title: Chechen Republic
capsule: The Chechen Republic (Нохчийчоь, Noxçiyçö) re-emerged as a distinct administrative unit within the Russian Federation following the dissolution of the Chechen-Ingush ASSR in 1992, but its political status was violently contested across two federal wars. The First Chechen War (1994–1996) ended with the Khasavyurt Accords leaving effective Chechen self-governance in place; the Second Chechen War began in September 1999 after Chechen incursions into Dagestan and apartment bombings in Russian cities attributed to Chechen militants. Federal forces recaptured Grozny in early 2000 after devastating bombardment, and Akhmad Kadyrov was installed as head of administration in 2000, assassinated in 2004; his son Ramzan Kadyrov subsequently consolidated authoritarian control and the republic was formally reintegrated into the Russian federal system, removing the de facto separatist government by 2006.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Chechen Republic's administrative boundaries are well documented, but the extent of separatist versus federal control at any given point in 1992–2006 fluctuated with the military situation and is the subject of contested documentation.
